sections.teaching:
Professor Shen's teaching is very good, he explains the ideas very well. Sometimes in some "hard" topic he will even slow down the pace for fear that some students cannot catch up the contents.

Also Professor Shen is very nice and happy to answer our questions after class. Emails he will almost reply immediately.

Don't know how the TA teaches, I just escape all TA lectures. I only watch video and realise that they don't turn on microphone.

I see one TA in lab, can speak in cantonese, he is really helpful and reliable. Since some of TAs don't know how to do the lab, lab sessions every questions and management are resolved by that TA.
sections.grading:
By default Professor Shen wants to give only 10% A-range. However, I persuade him to maximize the grade according to ARRO (25% A-range, 40% B-range, remaining C-range). But so far we don't know the final grade. Welcome to comment after releasing the final grade to guess the grading boundaries.

Updated: Some classmate only above UQ 1 mark in both exams and get A. The grading is very good and maximized! 🛐

The contents are quite easy. Also for open book open notes exams, we can prepare for everything like cheatsheet, calculator programs, printed materials. Prepare well is very critical!

Here is my score:
HW1: 4.9/5
HW2: 4.75/5
HW3: 4.8/5
HW4: 5/5
HW is quite time consuming, but is totally manageable.
Especially for HW1, modelling is quite difficult. However luckily the most difficult question is modified inverted pendulum, which we can copy from the lab manual.
For HW2 and HW3, Professor Shen makes many of block diagram simplification. The large computation maybe easily to get wrong >.<. This part should check those questions multiple times, also cross check with friends (But no friends can check with me 〒▽〒.)

Midterm Exam: 27.5/30
LQ: 17.5
Mean: 20.6
Median: 22.5
UQ: 25
High: 30
SD: 5.96
Midterm exam is very trivial, all of questions are same type as past paper or in homework. A little bit more computation is for modelling and block diagram simplification. However the modelling is just simple electric circuit dry run, which is very easy in terms of physics.
The remaining question is laplace transform with partial fractions, rough table, controller design. I used calculator programs to finish those 3 big questions within only 10 minutes...

Final Exam: 49/50
LQ: 25.5
Mean: 33.93
Median: 35.2
UQ: 41.1
High: 49
SD: 9.07
Final exam some questions are kind of difficult. Especially for the modelling question, which is integrated by circuit and mechanical system with considering moment of inertia. At last need to do linearization. Everything are derived from scratch, which is very likely to make mistakes or mess up the later part.

Also the last question about root-locus method is not merely computing root-locus. You need to derive the model equations and transfer function about a drone（無人機）, the deviation is luckily very similar with HW3 last question modelling.

The remaining is block diagram simplification, controller design (solving linear equation which can be done in calculator, even can be solved by hand since many leading entries are 1), PID controller and finding output given some input. Trivial but maybe time consuming because of the long computation.

The time is very sufficient, 3 hours final exam. Only the modelling question and root locus function derivation consumes huge amount of time (more than 1 hour). But can remain 1 hour for checking. Many questions are very easy to get wrong and mess up, prepare well by installing calculator programs, in additional should redo the whole question to prevent any careless mistake.

I see many classmates felt not good after exam. But surprising the median still kept as 70%, seems the middle 3 questions saved many classmates.

Lab bonus: 4.05/5
Only need to pass the demo is enough to get 2.5 bonus points for each lab, maximum 5 points for 2 labs.
They deduct my score from 5 points to 4.05 points because they want to crop my overall score into 100.
sections.workload:
Low workload, only need to go lectures, even can skip because they have lecture videos.

Lab and HW can use AI, except modelling and block diagram simplification.

Since TAs in Labs are even puzzled how to finish lab tasks. They didn't manage the lab well. You only need to input the parameters of controller in Matlab which everything else are all implemented. (Doesn't deny that you can directly copy the previous student's data). And click a button and do simulation. You pass, then you can leave and +2.5 overall score.

Every lecture only have 1-2 main points. For example, the whole Laplace transform only needs to care about final value theorem formula and DC gain.

Only 3 moderate to difficult topics.
1. The most difficult part is modelling, very sufficient knowledge of PHYS1112, PHYS1114 and ELEC2400 are required.
The sign convention will totally fked up if we mess up.

2. Then is block diagram simplification. Easy to get mistakes.

3. The last one is root locus method, many rules and some of them maybe abstract for some students.

Other can either be solved by calculator programs (FX-50/FX-3650P etc). Like rough table and solving linear equations. Or is extremely simple like DC gain.

The overall workload is quite low.

sections.content:
This is a broad elective from the ELEC 3000 series (which you may have realised coz of all the prerequisites for this course).

This course involves a lot of calculations requiring skills from solving differential equation sets to Laplace Transform to calculating signal NORM. (it's nothing really, coz in the exam you are allowed to use MATLAB to solve pretty much everything.)

Majority of the course is on finding overall system transfer functions and relationships between system variables & coefficients. Optimization was taught mostly in the last part but is also involved in the 1st & 2nd labs so its advised to really read through the content and get to know what you are about to handle.

If your mathematics / logic skills are not that good, or you seldom attend classes,  DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE.

Assignments require writing matlab codes for pole placements and such. If you know the concept it is quite simple, however if youre not particularly good in MATLAB that's another story.

Overall, the concepts taught in this course requires time to digest.
